Describe the project as an enlargement of the existing Pacific Catch restaurant from 689 to 1,378 sq ft by merging storefronts within parcel 0491/001, with limited cooking, no change to hours (closing at 11 p.m.), no alcohol service addition, and no entertainment. outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS. What to say: File LLC Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1, $70) or general stock corporation articles (Form ARTS-GS, $100) online at the Secretary of State's bizfile portal. Apply for an EIN at irs.gov the same day (free, issued immediately Monday–Friday). The EIN and entity name are prerequisites for the San Francisco business registration, the seller's permit, the bank account, and the lease.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and a California Seller's Permit. What to say: Register online with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector (fee is tiered by gross receipts, starting at $55 plus $4 state fee); the registration year runs April 1 to March 31. Register for the seller's permit at the CDTFA website the same week (free, often issued same day). Every other city permit asks for the Business Account Number (BAN), so complete this step before filing building or health permits.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check and building permit applications concurrently, with 'health' as a routing station on the DBI application. What to say: File the DPH plan check online at least one month before the target opening date, attaching scaled drawings, interior/exterior photos, menu, and equipment list. The FY2026–27 fee for a new restaurant plan check is $2,207 (8 hours at $276/hour). File the building permit application at DBI with the architect's stamped plans, making sure 'health' is checked as a routing station so the two reviews proceed in parallel. The building permit will be routed to Planning under Section 175(a) for zoning sign-off.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After DPH approves the plans, schedule the pre-final and final DPH inspections and the DBI final inspection. What to say: Book the DPH pre-final inspection at ~80% construction complete and the final inspection at 100% complete, calling your DPH plan reviewer at least two weeks ahead for each. Walk the space against the DPH checklist (hand sinks, sealed surfaces, hot water, grease interceptor) a week before the final to avoid failed inspections. The health permit to operate is issued after the final inspection passes and you show proof of a certified food safety manager on staff.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain workers' compensation insurance, register for EDD payroll taxes, enroll employees in food handler card training, and certify one food safety manager. What to say: Quote workers' comp through a broker or State Fund before the first employee is hired (mandatory from day one). Register online with EDD e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying wages (free). Enroll all food-handling employees in an ANSI-accredited food handler card course ($7–$15, valid 3 years) within 30 days of hire. At least one owner or employee must pass an accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe or equivalent, ~$125–$200, valid 5 years) before the DPH final inspection.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $4,600 to $21,000. Notes: The timeline and cost are for approval of the Conditional Use Authorization and health permit to operate, assuming formula retail status is confirmed and a CUA hearing is required. The CUA typically takes 120–300 days from application to final approval (including pre-application meeting, environmental review, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period); the health permit plan check and permit to operate add 35–105 days in parallel with the building permit. Government fees: CUA application ~$3,100 (adjusted annually for CPI; was $2,747 in 2023–24), building permit $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation, DPH plan check $828–$2,500 (new restaurant is typically $2,207 for 8 hours), health permit to operate $470 application plus $0 annual license for restaurants in FY2026–27, business registration $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts, and sign permit $300–$1,500. If Pacific Catch is determined to be non-formula retail, the CUA is not required and the timeline drops to 14–120 days (building permit plus health permit in parallel), with government fees of ~$1,500–$18,500. The figures above do not include architectural, legal, or construction costs, which are not government fees.
